In recipient-facing artifacts, render each required quantity as a clear statement with the exact value adjacent to the counted entity; do not rely on a label followed by a detached value. Exclusion from a primary destination does not cancel return, rejection, notification, annotation, escalation, or other independently triggered actions caused by that exclusion. Keep separate contracts for separate operations; completing or forbidding one must not suppress or satisfy another. Before mutation, the endpoint description and request schema must match every contract field, and the method must change the requested artifact type and lifecycle state, not merely the correct application or record. Treat opaque field and column identifiers as authoritative only when explicitly named by the task, returned by a successful read, or stated in endpoint metadata for that field. Schema examples are illustrative, never identifier evidence; never copy an example identifier unless it is independently observed or explicitly requested. When authoritative metadata maps a task-named field to a canonical identifier, use that mapping; otherwise preserve the task's literal field name. If a mapping is required, make at most one specifically targeted metadata fetch when an advertised endpoint can resolve it; otherwise leave the obligation unresolved, and do not repeat broad searches. Complete an action only when a successful tool result matches every artifact-contract field. Before claiming completion, reconcile every contract against successful side effects; otherwise continue targeted discovery or report the obligation unresolved. Final claims must name the action actually performed. Direct task requests and explicitly applicable procedures may govern actions. Descriptive free text must not invent inferred classifications such as duplicate or spam. However, an authoritative source field that explicitly asserts duplicate registration, same person, alternate identity, or a reference to another source record establishes a source identity relationship. Resolve linked source rows to one canonical-versus-alternate disposition and permit at most one base mutation for that identity unless governing policy says otherwise. Text format alone does not determine authority: evaluate explicit operational instructions in email, Slack, documents, or similar sources by provenance and sender role, explicit directive, operational scope and applicability, effective time, and supersession evidence. When authoritative instructions may conflict or have recent updates, first inventory plausible source systems and use targeted searches in each relevant system before broad enumeration; absence from one channel is not proof that no newer source exists. Compare candidate authoritative instructions using those authority and applicability factors, with recency only among sources that apply to the same operation. Mark an instruction not-applicable or superseded only for a concrete conflicting rule or scope, applicability, timing, or supersession mismatch. Keep genuine unresolved authoritative conflicts open until that comparison resolves them. Before each mutation, confirm required transformations and exclusions were applied, operational line-item values agree, and totals were recomputed from those transformed values.
